subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The SolarWinds Supply Chain Attack
description: A fast breakdown of The SolarWinds Supply Chain Attack for builders.

hook.text: Hackers hid malware inside a trusted software update. 18,000 organizations installed it willingly.

buildup.text: SolarWinds made network management software used by governments and Fortune 500 companies worldwide.

discovery.text: Russian hackers inserted a backdoor into a SolarWinds update, gaining access to US Treasury and Pentagon systems.

twist.text: The attack went undetected for nine months. Victims trusted the update because it came from a trusted vendor.

climax.text: SolarWinds proved that the biggest threat isn't the front door — it's the trusted supply chain.

punchline.text: A trusted update. A hidden backdoor. Nine months.

quiz.question: What made the SolarWinds attack so effective?
options: Malware was hidden in a trusted software update
